cards.p: A guest asks if [dish] can be made [vegan, mild, smaller]. Reply in my voice using my notes: [notes].
A guest says their order was wrong: [paste]. Reply with one sorry and the fix we offer. No excuses.
Write a waitlist text: table for [name] ready in [minutes], we hold it [minutes], reply 1 to keep it.
Write a post and an auto reply: closed [day] because [reason], back [date], how to order ahead.
Write a catering quote for [guests] people on [date]: menu [items], price per head [price], deposit, setup time.
A party of [number] wants [day]. Reply with a set menu, a [amount] deposit, and one backup time.
Write a short email to the office manager at [company] offering a free tasting of our lunch trays on [date].
Turn this catering order into a checklist: food, amounts, packing, setup time, who drives: [paste].
Reply to this review saying the food arrived cold: [paste]. Own it, do not blame the driver, under 60 words.
A regular praises [staff] in this review: [paste]. Thank them, credit [staff], invite them to try [new dish].
Rank the dishes in these reviews by praise and complaints: [paste]. Give one fix per complaint.
Write a small table card asking guests for a Google review. One warm line, a QR code spot, no reward.
Write today's location post for my food truck or pop up: [spot], hours [hours], two specials, how to order ahead.
Write a post launching [new dish]: what is in it, why we made it, price [price], first day [date].
We sold out of [dish] by [time]. Write a story post: thanks, when it returns, how to get it first.
Give me 3 short video ideas showing how we make [dish], each with a hook for the first 2 seconds.
Sort these supplier bills by produce, meat, dry goods, drinks, packaging: [paste]. Total each. Flag repeats.
Here are my ingredient costs for [dish]: [paste]. What does one plate cost me, and what is left at [price]?
Catering invoice [amount] for [event] is [X] days late. Write a polite text: pay by date and [link].
Turn this week's waste notes into a table by item and reason: [paste]. What should I prep less of?
Turn my menu and [number] expected covers into tomorrow's prep list, by station: [paste menu].
Turn how I make [dish] into a recipe card a new cook can follow: amounts, steps, plating, time.
Turn tonight's notes into a handover for the morning crew: what ran out, what broke, what to prep: [paste].
Write a 2 minute pre shift brief: specials [list], sold out items [list], and one goal for tonight.
